newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia sees better electronic goods demand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia sees better electronic goods demand.

text.p: Demand for electrical and electronic goods is expected to rise in the final quarter of 1996, Malaysia's International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz said on Monday.
The recent drop in demand for semiconductor goods was not worrying, as the market for such items was cyclical, she was quoted as saying by the national Bernama news agency.
"The process has also indirectly forced the companies to enhance their high technology and produce high quality products which will boost the market price for locally-manufactured goods," she said.

The country's semiconductor exports dropped to 9.0 billion ringgit in the second quarter of this year from 9.2 billion in the first quarter, Rafidah said, adding that as of September 30, 31 factories or 3.2 per cent of the total electronic factories in the country closed down.
The industry was also undergoing a rationalisation process to compete more aggressively in the international market and to be more prepared to face future challenges, she said.
